decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display, it remains very close to the firm's core POS offer and still supports its service-led problem-solving positioning.
The pegboard-back cardboard display is still a standard in-store variant that fits the firm's established manufacturing strengths and helps cover customer needs within a focused range.
This generic cardboard quarter-pallet display overlaps with other formats, but it is a core staple of the firm's narrow portfolio and is still worth retaining unless newer developments replace it.
The wooden display pallet is less central to a paper-based display specialist's core range, so releasing its resources for core cardboard solutions and new development is the better choice.

The media-oriented quarter-pallet display is a relatively niche variant with weaker long-term fit than the firm's broader cardboard display lines, making withdrawal the more likely management decision.
